$comment: Canonical AiFinPay B2BSplitter registry — the single source of truth for the
addresses the SDK pays. The SDK's table is GENERATED from this file; never
hand-edit the generated copy, CI compares the two and fails on drift.
KEYED BY CHAIN AND ROUTE. From v1.3 a chain carries one splitter per protocol
route, because the fee split is immutable at construction and the two
protocols need different economics. A key is '<chain>:<route>' and selection
must use both. Never resolve a splitter by chain alone and never fall back
from one route to the other: the deployer used CREATE, so the same address
recurs on different chains for different routes — OP's merchant-aifp1 is the
same address as Base's agent-x402 — and an address alone therefore says
nothing about which economics apply.
'verified' records what was read FROM THE CHAIN on the stated date: the
deployed bytecode was fetched, the payment entrypoint selector was found in
it, and runtimeCodeHash is the keccak-256 of that exact bytecode. A missing
or stale runtimeCodeHash fails verification — an address alone says nothing
about what is deployed at it.
An unreachable RPC is NOT a pass. verify-registry.mjs exits non-zero when it
cannot reach a required chain, because 'we could not check' and 'it is fine'
must never produce the same result.
Version semantics: v1.1 exposes payMatic(address,address,string);
v1.2 payNative(bytes32,address,address,string);
v1.3 payNative((bytes32,address,uint256,address,uint256,string)) — tuple
argument, and GROSS-INCLUSIVE: the payer's amount already contains the fee.
Route semantics under v1.3:
merchant-aifp1 (100/0) — the agent pays the quoted gross amount, the
AiFinPay treasury receives 1%, the merchant receives 99%.
agent-x402 (0/0) — the provider receives 100% of the provider-defined
price and the AiFinPay fee is 0% for now. This route is NOT fee-on-top.
Fee-on-top, provider-preserving semantics arrive in a future contract
version when the AIFP-2 fee is activated; do not describe today's route
that way and do not convert this contract to it.
Entries marked superseded are retained deliberately. Historical deployments
are evidence and are never deleted; settlement on them stays disabled.

notSplitters.$comment: Recorded so nobody mistakes a Core deployment for a payment target. Neither exposes payMatic or payNative — paying these would not settle.

$policyFields: validFrom and validUntil are a POLICY review window, not chain state. They
cannot be read from a contract, so they are declared here and must be
renewed deliberately. An expired window fails validateQuotedNativePayment
with registry_entry_expired, which is intended: a route nobody has
re-reviewed should stop settling rather than drift on.
The window is 90 days from registry activation. Renewal and review are owned
by the Web3/CTO side under Governance Safe control.
settlementEnabled is deliberately false on every v1.3 entry at activation.
Deployed and verified is not the same as payable. A chain and route is
enabled individually, and only after a successful mainnet paid end-to-end
settlement on that exact route with verified balance deltas.
